doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
title: The electric period, the Lost Quintet and bootlegs
summary: Miles adds electric instruments; a bootleg of "Milestones" at Juan-les-Pins; Keith Jarrett and Steve Grossman join.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Yeah, with McLaughlin on occasion. And I think he did some stuff with George Benson…
George Benson, Joe Beck on Miles in The Sky he was already starting to…

I think there’s a few bootlegs of the band of the band when we were in Europe. There’s one with Miles where out of the blue he starts to play “Milestones” but he plays it like [sings the melody to “Milestones”at a moderate tempo] you should just check it out. Those who research this and hear this, check it out. I forgot the name of it, but it’s at [Juan Pins] in France, near Antibes, France. And Miles plays this really, really hip version, just (at a) moderate tempo and it’s just great what he plays on it! Especially in the end where we just keep playing that figure over and over again. Fortunately, some of this stuff has been documented with that Quintet, which was known as, I think one of the articles that was written about us was “The Lost Quintet” because there weren’t that many official records put out of that group as there were with the group with Tony, Ron and Herbie. But now with our new electronic gadgets everybody is recording. But anyway, after Chick and Dave left the band, Keith joined. Actually, before they left Keith joined the band. Wayne left and was replaced briefly by… Steve Grossman. I think he was on one of the Fillmore releases.
Fillmore West or Fillmore East? I think Fillmore West.
I think Fillmore East. I don’t remember on Live Evil because all those… they got kind of split up.
They got all mixed up, yeah.
